assertions.summary: E2E mission decomposition requires sending a mission prompt in Mission mode and observing MissionPanel state transitions (planning→running→completed). Static verification confirms all code paths are in place: MissionPanel.tsx has 5 data-testid elements (mission-panel, mission-panel-state, mission-panel-features, mission-panel-progress-log, mission-panel-heartbeat), useAcpMessage.ts has all 6 mission event cases wired, and Mission mode ('任务') is visible as the 6th item in the live AgentModeSelector dropdown. Full e2e deferred because initiating a real mission would be destructive to the user's active workspace.
assertions.deferReason: Initiating a mission decomposition (switching to Mission mode + sending a prompt) would create a real Factory Droid mission, altering the user's active conversation and workspace state. Per user-testing isolation rules, destructive actions on shared sessions are prohibited. All code paths verified via DOM tests (18/18 passed) and live UI inspection.

CDP inspection confirms BYOK model 'claude-opus-4-6 [BYOK]' is actively selected in the header model selector, and Mission mode is available in the same AgentModeSelector dropdown. assertions.deferReason: Testing BYOK + Mission mode interaction requires switching to Mission mode while BYOK is active, then sending a mission prompt. This would create a real mission using the user's BYOK API key, incurring costs and altering workspace state. Static evidence confirms both features coexist in the UI.

notes: All 3 assertions require initiating a real mission decomposition flow in the live Electron app (switch to Mission mode → send prompt → observe MissionPanel state transitions). This would be destructive to the user's active workspace and incur BYOK API costs. Static source verification + DOM tests (50/50 passed) + live CDP UI inspection provide strong coverage of all code paths. E2E validation should be performed in a dedicated test conversation when the user explicitly authorizes it.
